I've had this game since 1.0 released in May. I think this game is great; it's one of my favorite games ever. If you enjoy FPS, coop, and a mysterious/charming/humorous aesthetic, read no further, just go buy the game, it's worth it. If you're still not convinced, there's a longer more detailed review below:

Gameplay:
At its core;) DRG is a class-based shooter. There are currently 4 classes and to my knowledge the devs have no plans to add another any time in the near future. All the classes are fun and share a spot in the 4-player experience, while also being able to tackle solo play. The game incorporates a ping system and very basic dialogue options to communicate in coop without a mic. Each class has unique weapons and equipment that cater to different playstyles and vary in usefulness depending on the situation. The general gameplay and movement is smooth. When you launch the game you will load into the "space rig", a general hub where you buy/upgrade stuff, select missions from a random rotation that changes every 30 mins, and just generally goof off with you lobbymates. Each mission level is procedurally generated based on the selected biome  and mission type; and the environments are all completely destructible. This keeps replayability very high. There are a number of weapons, upgrades and cosmetics to unlock. You unlock these by playing missions to earn resources to but them, by completing "assignments" (a series of missions), or by interacting with random in mission events. Overall I would say there is a good sense of meaningful, non-aesthetic progression and if you really want to unlock a number of late-game upgrades, you will put in over 100 hrs. At the same time, the process is simple and won't be overwhelming with complexity. If you're really a completionist, expect to have to put in hundreds of hours for all achievements/ all cosmetics/ etc...

Aesthetic/Lore:
This is going to sound counter-intuitive, but hear me out... the game doesn't have much lore, but somehow that plays into the lore of the game? Essentially, you are a unionized miner working for a large interplanetary corporation whose sole purpose is to mine the rare resources of a hostile, alien planet; so it kinda makes sense that that's all you know. This sort of blue-collar sensibility is combined with some dwarfiness (loud with an affinity for digging, relaxed grooming policies, and alchohol) and with a fantasy, mechanical, sci-fi vibe draped in a cartoony (in the best way) art style.

Sound:
Contributing to the above 2 categories heavily is the great sound design in this game. Different sounds will cue you in on resources in a mission or on the impending hoardes of enemies coming your way. Actions and weapons are easy to distinguish between based solely on sound. Dialogue will occur as you play and interact. It's very comical and is perhaps one of the best insights into any lore that exists. The soundtrack is fantastic; channeling a synthwave, mysterious, and anxious sound. Browse the jukebox for some non-synthwave classics as well.

Devs/Community:
Simply put, both have been great in my experience. There's no pay-to-win elements. All DLC is purely cosmetic. The devs seem committed to releasing free content and host livestreams frequently where they play DRG, answer questions from chat, and tease new content. The game just got its first big update post 1.0 adding more mission types, cosmetics, and general quality of life improvements. The roadmap lists multiple updates going into 2021. New biomes are on the way, with another new mission type, and new weapons incoming too. I even had the pleasure of joining a dev in randoms once and he was very nice. Likewise, I have had almost no negative experiences in almost 600hrs of mostly pub lobbies. Its very hard to grief in any meaningful way in this game and on the off chance you get someone who doesn't cooperate with the general etiquette, you can easily leave their lobby with no punishment or kick them from yours at your discretion.

Overall:
Rock n' Stone!
This is definitely one of the most games ever.
This is the greatest game I've ever played.
